"""A short-context quantity and selection detector.

Numbers in words and indefinite selectors ('one', 'some', 'each', 'both', etc.)
usually give a negative signal. Context offsets distinguish standalone or
coordinated selections from prepositional uses. 'Of' and following pronouns get
separate partitive offsets. A few related determiners, fractions and translated
quantifiers are included; minor rules cover percent signs and the literal None.
It keeps only the previous two tokens, resetting at document boundaries; it does not attempt a grammatical parse.
"""

import inflect

READS = ()
_english = inflect.engine()
_CARDINALS = ' '.join(_english.number_to_words(i) for i in range(2, 21))
_ORDINALS = ' '.join(_english.number_to_words(_english.ordinal(i))
                     for i in range(2, 11))

# Named word classes: (activation offset, member words).
CLASSES = {
    'one': (-1.316, 'one'),
    'small_number': (-0.603, _CARDINALS),
    'some': (-1.306, 'some'),
    'many': (-0.850, 'many'),
    'few': (-1.021, 'few'),
    'several': (-0.612, 'several'),
    'any': (-0.358, 'any'),
    'each': (-0.627, 'each'),
    'every': (-0.212, 'every'),
    'all': (-0.210, 'all'),
    'both': (-0.433, 'both'),
    'either': (-0.084, 'either neither'),
    'other': (-0.258, 'other another'),
    'others': (-0.579, 'others'),
    'none': (-1.122, 'none'),
    'null_literal': (-0.353, ''),
    'most': (-0.122, 'most'),
    'first': (-0.089, 'first'),
    'ordinal': (-0.199, _ORDINALS),
    'former': (-0.277, 'former latter'),
    'these': (0.096, 'these'),
    'those': (-0.367, 'those'),
    'half': (-0.333, 'half'),
    'remaining': (-0.266, 'rest'),
    'ones': (-0.756, 'ones'),
    'whole': (0.216, 'whole entire'),
    'percent': (-0.238, 'percent % ％ ٪'),
    'multitude': (-0.288, 'multiple numerous various hundreds thousands millions'),
    'romance_one': (-1.040, 'uno una uma'),
    'foreign_article': (-0.148, 'un une um ein eine einen einem einer eines één'),
    'slavic_one': (-1.252, 'один одна одно одну'),
    'foreign_some': (-1.175,
        'algunos algunas alguns algumas quelques '
        'einige einigen mehrere mehreren بعض'),
    'foreign_each': (-0.275, 'jeder jede jedem jeden jedes chaque cada ogni каждый каждая'),
    'foreign_all': (-0.292, 'tutti tutte todas todos tous beide beiden'),
    'digits': (-0.021, ""),
    'han_one': (-0.448, ""),
    'han_some': (-0.663, ""),
    'han_each': (-0.062, ""),
}
WORDS = {w: name for name, (_, words) in CLASSES.items() for w in words.split()}
STRONG = {'one', 'small_number', 'some', 'many', 'few', 'several'}
SELECTORS = set(CLASSES) - {
    'most', 'these', 'those', 'whole', 'null_literal', 'percent',
    'digits', 'han_one', 'han_some', 'han_each',
}
PREPOSITIONS = set(
    'of in at for on to from by into with within over under about upon'.split())
DETERMINERS = set(
    'the a an this that these those his her its their our your my'.split())
CONJUNCTIONS = {'and', 'or', 'but', 'nor'}
NEGATION = {'no', 'not', 'never', 'without'}

def category(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if token.strip() == 'None':
        return 'null_literal'
    if word.rstrip('),.;') in {'%', '％', '٪'}:
        return 'percent'
    if word in WORDS:
        return WORDS[word]
    if word and word.isdecimal():
        return 'digits'
    # Chinese indefinite amounts, and one followed by a measure word.
    if word.startswith((
        '一些', '有些', '不少', '若干', '几', '幾', '数个', '數個',
        '多个', '多個', '许多', '許多', '有的',
    )):
        return 'han_some'
    if word.startswith((
        '一个', '一個', '一位', '一名', '一条', '一條', '一只', '一隻',
        '一项', '一項', '一股', '一枚', '一种', '一種', '一批', '一组', '一組',
    )):
        return 'han_one'
    if word.startswith(('每', '各')):
        return 'han_each'
    return ''

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    history = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else []
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    prev = history[-1] if history else ''
    p = prev.strip().lower()
    c = category(token)
    # Do not mistake a word's suffix for a free English determiner.
    inside_word = (token and token[0].isalpha() and prev and prev[-1].isalpha())
    if inside_word and not c.startswith('han_'):
        c = ''
    value = 0.003 + CLASSES.get(c, (0.0, ""))[0]
    comma = any(ch in prev for ch in ',;:')
    if c in SELECTORS or c.startswith('han_'):
        strong = c in STRONG
        if p in PREPOSITIONS:
            value += (0.085 if strong else 0.196)
        if p in DETERMINERS:
            value += (0.232 if strong else -0.139)
        if p in CONJUNCTIONS:
            value += (-0.774 if strong else -0.094)
        if comma:
            value += (-0.782 if strong else -0.399)
        if not history or any(ch in prev for ch in '.!?\n'):
            value += (-0.461 if strong else -0.209)
        if p in NEGATION:
            value += (0.672 if strong else -0.421)
        if token.lstrip()[:1].isupper():
            value += (0.150 if strong else 0.063)
        if p in {'which', 'what', 'whichever'}:
            value += (-0.819 if strong else -0.250)
        if p in {'have', 'has', 'had', 'be', 'is', 'are', 'was', 'were'}:
            value += (-0.285 if strong else -0.224)
        if c == 'one' and comma:
            value += -0.540
    if c == 'these' and token.lstrip()[:1].isupper():
        value += -0.415
    if word == 'of':
        pc = category(prev)
        if pc in SELECTORS or pc == 'digits':
            if pc == 'one':
                value += -0.867
            elif pc == 'some':
                value += -0.728
            elif pc in STRONG or pc == 'digits':
                value += -0.660
            else:
                value += -0.174
            if len(history) > 1 and any(ch in history[-2] for ch in ',;:'):
                value += -1.019
    if word in {'which', 'whom'} and p == 'of':
        value += -1.106
    if word == 'least' and p == 'at':
        value += 0.376
    return (doc, (history + [token])[-2:]), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1344 -- a "how many / which ones" quantity-word detector.

What it does: this component goes strongly negative on quantity words that stand for a
count of things, used as the head of a phrase: "one" and "some" most of all ("one of
them", "some are used"), then "many", "few", "each", "several", "two" to "nine", "none",
"both", "others". Indefinite quantifiers "any", "all", "another", "those" are weaker.
Numbers from ten up do nothing, and "hundred", "million" do nothing.

It is weaker when the quantity word follows a preposition or determiner ("at some point",
"in one", "for many"), and it is also negative on the "of" right after a quantity word
("one of", "many of"). Everything else predicts 0.

The program predicts the activation from the current token and the one before it. It keeps
no state, and it resets at a document boundary.
"""

# How negative the component goes on each quantity word, in activation units.
QUANTITY = {
    "one": 1.5, "some": 1.5, "many": 1.0, "few": 0.9, "each": 0.6, "none": 0.5,
    "several": 0.7, "others": 0.6, "ones": 0.6, "both": 0.45, "another": 0.4,
    "two": 0.7, "three": 0.65, "four": 0.6, "five": 0.6, "six": 0.7, "seven": 0.65,
    "eight": 0.65, "nine": 0.6, "any": 0.35, "all": 0.2, "those": 0.35,
    "second": 0.35, "third": 0.35, "half": 0.35,
    # the same idea in Spanish, French, German and Italian
    "una": 0.9, "uno": 1.1, "algunos": 1.5, "einige": 1.1,
}

# A quantity word right after one of these is a weaker, mid-phrase use ("at some point").
WEAK_AFTER = {
    "at", "on", "in", "for", "within", "during", "over", "under", "across", "through",
    "above", "after", "no", "a", "every",
}

OF_AFTER = 0.5  # the "of" in "one of", "many of", as a fraction of the quantity word's value

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    prev = ""
    if len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    if word == "of" and prev in QUANTITY:
        return None, -OF_AFTER * QUANTITY[prev]
    if word not in QUANTITY:
        return None, 0.0
    scale = 0.4 if prev in WEAK_AFTER else 1.0
    return None, -QUANTITY[word] * scale

"""Sparse responses to document openings and two web-boilerplate phrases.

An opening '12' gives a large positive response on its second digit.
An opening 'Title' gives a positive response, followed by a negative one
if the next token is a colon. 'Wiki User' and 'new seq' give smaller
positive responses on their second tokens. Everything else is zero:
this captures selected spikes, not the diffuse background activity.
"""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        previous, position = '', 0
    else:
        _, previous, position = carry
        position += 1

    value = 0.0
    if position == 1 and previous == '1' and token == '2':
        value = 4.0
    elif position == 0 and token == 'Title':
        value = 0.727
    elif position == 1 and previous == 'Title' and token == ':':
        value = -1.564
    elif previous == 'Wiki' and token == ' User':
        value = 1.04
    elif previous == ' new' and token == ' seq':
        value = 0.83
    return (doc, token, position), value

"""Document-opening "1 2" detector, with a weak first-token effect, for
layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1346.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Main effect: when a document opens with the two characters "1" then "2", the digit "2"
  (the document's second token) gets a large positive value, about +4. This is the
  component's peak; in the training data it fires only in this case.
- Weak effect: the document's first token gets a small signed value: +0.25 for a special
  chat or end marker such as <|im_start|>, and -0.06 for a token that begins with a space
  (a mid-sentence continuation). Other first tokens get 0.
- Everywhere else it predicts 0. Its real activation there is a small, diffuse,
  token-specific value (about +-0.05) that no short rule captures.

A document starts at the row's first token or where document_ids changes, as the model
resets there.
"""

READS = ()

SPIKE = 4.0          # "1" then "2" at the start of a document
SPECIAL_START = 0.25  # first token is a special marker such as <|im_start|>
SPACE_START = -0.06   # first token begins with a space


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    # carry = (document id, index where the current document starts in this row)
    start = t if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    carry = (doc, start)
    token = prefix.token_strings[t]
    if t == start:
        if token.startswith("<|"):
            return carry, SPECIAL_START
        if token.startswith(" "):
            return carry, SPACE_START
        return carry, 0.0
    if t - start == 1 and prefix.token_strings[start] == "1" and token == "2":
        return carry, SPIKE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer-1 MLP down_proj component 1347.

Mostly silent. Two behaviours:
1. The token '··' (two middle dots, the dot-leader filler of tables of contents and
   forms) gives about +1.17 wherever it appears. This is the largest, most
   consistent response.
2. The first token of each document (where attention and positions restart) gets a
   small positive value on average, +0.07. Its exact size depends on the token
   itself (for example, uppercase shouting words are negative, code symbols are
   positive), but that token dependence is only weakly captured by simple rules.

Everywhere else it predicts 0; the rest of its activity is small, diffuse, and
has no sign that a simple rule captures.
"""

READS = ()

DOC_START_VALUE = 0.07


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if token == "··":
        return carry, 1.17
    starts_doc = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    return carry, DOC_START_VALUE if starts_doc else 0.0

"""Detector for the sex / session / season / possession word family, in any script."""
import re

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# (pattern on lowercased recent text, activation). A match counts only if it ends inside
# the current token, so the value lands on the token that completes the word.
PATTERNS = (
    (re.compile(r"会话"), -10.0),                  # Chinese for session
    (re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])sess"), -5.0),        # session, sessions, Session
    (re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])sex"), -4.5),         # sex, sexual, sexe, sexo, SEX
    (re.compile(r"(?<![a-z])saison|(?<![a-z])season"), -2.5),  # season, saison
    (re.compile(r"possession"), -3.5),             # possession
    (re.compile(r"possess"), -1.5),                # possess, possesses
    (re.compile(r"сесс"), -4.0),                   # Russian сессия (session)
)
RECENT = 40  # characters of decoded text kept as context

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    new_doc = len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    recent = "" if new_doc or carry is None else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    text = (recent + token)[-RECENT:]
    value = 0.0
    for pattern, strength in PATTERNS:
        for m in pattern.finditer(text):
            if m.end() > len(text) - len(token):
                value = strength
    return text, value

programs.sol:
"""A small surface-form approximation, with a separate document-initial regime.

At document starts, English word shape and grammatical class matter much more
than elsewhere; study and research headings get a positive response. Later
predictions stay near zero except for a few Chinese lexical triggers, citation
notation, and the corpus's <filename> marker.
These are separate observed responses, not one claimed semantic category.
"""
import re
import regex

READS = ()

ARTICLES = set('a an the'.split())
DEMONSTRATIVES = set('this that these those'.split())
PERSONAL = set('i me we us you he him she her it they them'.split())
POSSESSIVE = set('my mine our ours your yours his hers its their theirs'.split())
BE = set('am is are was were be being been'.split())
STUDY_HEADINGS = set(
    'question problem practice lesson study learning science'.split())
RESEARCH_HEADINGS = set(
    'background abstract discussion review introduction'.split())


def initial_value(s):
    """Coarse spelling and function-word effects on a document's first token."""
    w = s.strip()
    low = w.lower()
    if s == '<|im_start|>':
        return 0.372
    if s == r'\t':
        return -1.797
    if s == r'\n':
        return -0.748
    if not s.startswith(' ') and low in STUDY_HEADINGS:
        return 1.25 + 0.30 * w.islower()
    if not s.startswith(' ') and low in RESEARCH_HEADINGS:
        return 1.0
    word = bool(re.fullmatch('[A-Za-z]+', w))
    value = 0.203 - 0.201 * s.startswith(' ') + 0.095 * ('\n' in s)
    value -= 0.278 * w.isdigit()
    value -= 0.099 * (bool(w) and all(not c.isalnum() for c in w))
    value -= 0.037 * bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', w))
    value -= 0.105 * bool(regex.search(
        r'[\p{Script=Hiragana}\p{Script=Katakana}]', w))
    if word:
        value -= 0.022
        value += 0.126 * w.isupper()
        value -= 0.191 * (len(w) == 1)
        value += 0.053 * (len(w) == 2)
        value += 0.154 * (len(w) >= 8)
        value -= 0.093 * (low in ARTICLES)
        value -= 0.314 * (low in DEMONSTRATIVES)
        value -= 0.221 * (low in PERSONAL)
        value -= 0.184 * (low in POSSESSIVE)
        value -= 0.099 * (low in BE)
        # Liquid consonant clusters, s-clusters, and common initial digraphs.
        value += 0.158 * bool(re.match('[bcdfgpt][rl]', low))
        value += 0.081 * bool(re.match('s[bcdfgklmnpqrtvwz]', low))
        value += 0.073 * low.startswith(('ch', 'sh', 'th', 'ph', 'wh'))
        value += 0.114 * low.startswith('qu')
        value += 0.211 * low.endswith('ion')
        value -= 0.145 * low.endswith('s')
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        n, recent = 0, ''
    else:
        _, n, recent = carry
    state = (doc, n + 1, (recent + s)[-32:])
    if n == 0:
        return state, initial_value(s)

    value = -0.001 - 0.012 * (n == 1) - 0.007 * (n == 2)
    # These lexical responses are restricted to the actual token spelling.
    if s == '岁月':                 # years / the passage of time
        value = 0.85
    elif s == '抗日':               # resistance to Japan
        value = 0.70
    elif s == '蜜':                 # honey
        value = 0.47
    elif s == '让更多':             # let more ...
        value = 0.62
    elif s == '豸':                 # the beast radical / character
        value = 1.0
    elif s == '期':                 # period or journal issue
        value = -1.5 if re.search(r'第\s*\d+$', recent) else -0.08
    elif s == 'filename' and n == 1 and recent == '<':
        value = -2.05
    elif s == '］' and re.search(r'[０-９]$', recent):
        value = -1.3
    elif s == '⋯' and recent.endswith('H'):
        value = -1.1                # dotted chemical bond, not ordinary ellipsis
    return state, float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1349 — a document-initial token detector with a small
token-shape rule.

What the component does, as far as a short program can say:
- Its activation is near zero almost everywhere (typical size about 0.04).
- Its largest values occur at the first token of a document (the first token after
  <|endoftext|>, or the first token of a row). There it is a few tenths to ~1.8, positive
  or negative, depending on which token it is.
- Away from document starts, the activation is diffuse and depends on the current token's
  identity in a way no short concept captures (a per-token table would explain about
  0.2 of the variance; no concept found does more than a few hundredths).

This program predicts the document-initial part only:
- At a document's first token, it adds a value built from simple token shape:
  the base is +0.125; a token that starts with a space is pushed down (-0.20); a
  token of 5 or more UTF-8 bytes is pushed up (+0.08); a bare-digit token is pushed
  down (-0.21); a special-marker or newline token is pushed up (+0.14); CJK characters
  nudge it down slightly (-0.02).
- Everywhere else it predicts 0.

The coefficients were fit by least squares on training rows (first half), and check
out on the other half. Its variance explained is small, and it barely moves the model's
next-token predictions, because switching the component off only has an effect at
non-initial positions, which this program leaves at zero.
"""

READS = ()


def _is_cjk(text):
    return any("一" <= ch <= "鿿" for ch in text)


def _document_start(prefix):
    """True at a row's first token or where the document label changes."""
    if prefix.position == 0:
        return True
    return prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if not _document_start(prefix):
        return carry, 0.0
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    stripped = text.strip()
    value = 0.125
    if text.startswith(" "):
        value -= 0.196
    if len(text.encode("utf-8")) >= 5:
        value += 0.081
    if stripped.isdigit():
        value -= 0.214
    if text.startswith("<") or "\n" in text:
        value += 0.139
    if _is_cjk(text):
        value -= 0.017
    return carry, float(value)

"""Stock-phrase completions.

The component fires on the token that finishes a memorised boilerplate string: a shebang line,
a licence header, a diff header, a URL or package path, a Rust attribute, a JavaScript
'use strict', a shell pipe in a tool call, or test-runner output. In each phrase the next token
is nearly forced by the template. The program keeps the recent text of the document and, when
it ends with one of these phrases, predicts that phrase's typical activation.
"""

READS = ()

# phrase (as text, ending at the firing token) -> typical activation there
PHRASES = {
    # script headers
    "usr/bin/env": 21.0,
    "#!/usr/bin": 1.4,
    # licence headers
    "shields.io/badge": 11.0,
    "under the License": 8.0,
    "THE SOFTWARE": 5.0,
    "SUCH DAMAGE": 6.0,
    "gnu.org/licenses": 6.9,
    "mozilla.org/MPL": 8.4,
    "This preview shows pages": 8.0,
    # code
    "use strict": 8.0,
    "#[derive": 6.5,
    "from __future": 10.0,
    "__author": 8.0,
    "__name": 1.6,
    "__main": 1.0,
    "<artifactId": 6.0,
    "css?family": 16.0,
    "node_modules": 2.1,
    "diff --git": 1.6,
    "+++ b": 6.4,
    "--- a": 1.0,
    "| grep": 2.5,
    # URLs
    "://github": 1.5,
    "github.com": 2.8,
    # test runner output
    "--- PASS": 1.2,
    "--- FAIL": 1.5,
    "=== RUN": 0.7,
}
TAIL = 60


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tail = carry or ""
    if len(prefix.document_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        tail = ""
    tail = (tail + prefix.token_strings[-1])[-TAIL:]
    value = 0.0
    for phrase, v in PHRASES.items():
        if tail.endswith(phrase):
            value = max(value, v)
    return tail, value

"""Opening of an anonymous function (callback, arrow function, lambda, block) in a value or
argument position.

Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1354 goes strongly negative on the token that opens a
function's header, just before its parameter list:
  - the keyword of a function value: `= function`, `: function`, `'x', function`,
    `= async`, `= func` (Go), `= lambda`, and glued forms like `click(function`;
  - the `(` or `()` that opens the parameters of an arrow function, e.g. `const f = (`,
    `'click', () =>`, `= async ()`, or a parenthesis after `catch`, `function` or `func`;
  - the `((` / `|` that opens a callback argument, e.g. `.map((`, `.then((`, `do |`.
Prose, declarations, ordinary parentheses and most other tokens stay near zero.

Predictions are the typical activation for each case, in the component's units: about -12 for
`= function`, -10 for other function keywords, -6 for empty parameter lists, -4 for a
parenthesis after catch/function, -5 for `const f = (`, and 0 elsewhere.
"""
READS = ()

FUNCTION_WORDS = ("function", "func", "async", "lambda")
# A value or an argument is expected after these characters (prose quotes and backticks are not).
VALUE_END = ("=", ":", ",", "(", "[", "{")
CALLBACK_BEFORE = ("catch", "then", "map", "forEach", "reduce", "filter", "click", "do")
DECLARATION_WORDS = ("const", "let", "var", "export")


def _core(token):
    """The token without its leading spaces, tabs and opening punctuation."""
    return token.lstrip(" \t(=:,['\"`{")


def _line_so_far(prefix):
    """The text of the current line before the token being predicted."""
    text = ""
    for piece in reversed(prefix.token_strings[:-1]):
        if "\n" in piece:
            break
        text = piece + text
    return text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].rstrip() if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
    after_value = prev[-1:] in VALUE_END

    # 1. the keyword that opens a function value: "= function", ":function", "click(function"
    if token[:1] in ("(", "=", ":") and _core(token) in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return carry, -8.0 if _core(token) == "lambda" else -10.0
    if token[:1] == " " and token[1:] in FUNCTION_WORDS and after_value:
        return carry, -12.0 if prev[-1:] == "=" else -10.0

What the component does, in plain terms:
  * It is mostly quiet (|activation| < 0.2 on ~99% of tokens).
  * It fires POSITIVE on the word "with" when "with" comes straight after a verb of
    working, testing, using or doing: "working with", "work with", "worked with",
    "Test with", "calculated with", "used with" (strongest for work/working, ~+2.5).
  * It is NEGATIVE on "with" after help/assist ("help with", "assist with", ~ -1.5).
  * It is NEGATIVE on punctuation that opens a label or heading: the colon or open
    parenthesis after a numbered label such as "Step 3:", "Test 2:", "Case 1:",
    "Proposition 1:", "Definition (", "Homework 1 (" (about -1.6 for colons), and a
    colon after a short capitalised heading line such as "Title:", "Last edited:",
    "Topic:" (strongest for edit/title/topic labels).
  * It is strongly NEGATIVE on a few web boilerplate tokens: "Originally [Posted] by"
    in forum quotes (~ -5), "View Full [Document]" (~ -10) and "This preview shows
    [pages]" (~ -10), which are rare but dominate the variance when they occur.
  * Markdown heading marks ("##", "###", "**") that start a numbered list item
    ("5. ##") are mildly negative.

text. It keeps no state between positions. Values are group means measured on
training rows, so the numbers are in activation units.

    # verbs of working / testing / calculating / using: "with" = "by means of, in dealing with"
    "work": 2.5, "working": 2.5, "worked": 2.5, "works": 2.5, "Working": 2.5, "Work": 2.5,
    "Worked": 2.5, "Works": 2.5,
    "Test": 1.5, "test": 1.5, "testing": 1.5, "Testing": 1.5, "calculated": 1.5,
    "obtained": 1.5, "practice": 1.5, "try": 1.5, "experiment": 1.5, "operate": 1.5,
    "properly": 1.5, "generated": 1.5, "conducted": 1.5, "produced": 1.5,
    "mostly": 1.5, "extensively": 1.5,
    "do": 0.5, "doing": 0.5, "did": 0.5, "done": 0.5, "made": 0.5, "use": 0.5,
    "used": 0.5, "performed": 0.5, "perform": 0.5,
    # "help with", "assist with": negative
    "help": -1.5, "helped": -1.5, "helping": -1.5, "helps": -1.5,
    "assist": -1.5, "assisting": -1.5, "assists": -1.5,
}
WITH_OTHER = 0.07           # any other "with"
NUMBERED_LABEL_COLON = -1.6  # "Step 3:", "Test 2:", "Case 1:"
NUMBERED_LABEL_PAREN = -0.7  # "Definition (" after a numbered label, "Homework 1 ("
NUMBERED_NUM_COLON = -0.3    # "at 5 :" style numbers after a lowercase word
HEADING_EDIT_COLON = -1.6    # "Last edited:", "Title:", "Topic:"
HEADING_COLON = -0.14        # other short capitalised heading line + ":"
HEADING_PAREN = -0.06        # short capitalised heading line + "("
OTHER_COLON = -0.04
BOILERPLATE = {              # (previous word, this token) -> activation
    ("Originally", " Posted"): -5.0,
    ("Full", " Document"): -10.0,
    ("shows", " pages"): -10.0,
}
MARKDOWN_HEADS = {" **", " ##", " ###", "##", "###"}
EDIT_WORDS = {"Edited", "Edit", "EDIT", "Topic", "Title"}
MARKDOWN_NUMLIST = -0.6


def is_number(text):
    return text.strip().isdigit()


def is_capitalised_word(text):
    text = text.strip()
    return text[:1].isupper() and text.isalpha()


def heading_line(strings, c, max_tokens=8):
    """Tokens since the last line break (or document start) before position c, and
    whether the line really starts at a break."""
    words = []
    j = c - 1
    while j >= 0 and len(words) < max_tokens:
        s = strings[j]
        if "\n" in s or "<|endoftext|>" in s or "<|im_" in s:
            break
        words.append(s)
        j -= 1
    at_start = j < 0 or "\n" in strings[j] or "<|endoftext|>" in strings[j] or "<|im_" in strings[j]

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    c = len(s) - 1
    x = s[c]
    p = s[c - 1] if c >= 1 else ""
    pp = s[c - 2] if c >= 2 else ""
    ppp = s[c - 3] if c >= 3 else ""
    value = 0.0
    if x == " with":
        value = WITH_AFTER.get(p.strip(), WITH_OTHER) if c >= 1 else 0.0
    elif x in (":", " ("):
        if is_number(p) and pp == " " and is_capitalised_word(ppp):
            value = NUMBERED_LABEL_COLON if x == ":" else NUMBERED_LABEL_PAREN
        elif is_number(p) and pp == " ":
            value = NUMBERED_NUM_COLON if x == ":" else 0.0
        else:
            line, at_start = heading_line(s, c)
            text = "".join(line).strip()
            if at_start and 1 <= len(line) <= 4 and text[:1].isupper():
                if x == ":" and any(w.strip() in EDIT_WORDS for w in line):
                    value = HEADING_EDIT_COLON
                else:
                    value = HEADING_COLON if x == ":" else HEADING_PAREN
            else:
                value = OTHER_COLON if x == ":" else 0.0
    if (p.strip(), x) in BOILERPLATE:
        value = BOILERPLATE[(p.strip(), x)]
    elif x in MARKDOWN_HEADS and (p.strip().endswith(".") or is_number(p.strip(". "))):
        value = MARKDOWN_NUMLIST

"""Statement keywords and assignments in source code.

The component fires on the tokens that open or perform a statement in program
code, not on the same words in English prose:

* `return` is strongest (about 2), then `break` (about 1.4), `throw` (1),
  `raise` and `continue` (weaker).
* The `=` of a simple assignment (`x = ...`, `const y = ...`) about 0.75,
  and Go's `:=` about 0.6.

A keyword counts only when its line so far is blank or contains code
punctuation (`{ } ; ( ) = [ ]`), so "to return" or "will break" in prose
predict 0. Escaped newlines (`\\n`) in code strings count as line breaks, and
a leading line-number gutter ("  123\\t") is ignored.
"""
import re

READS = ()

KEYWORD = {"return": 2.0, "break": 1.4, "throw": 1.0, "raise": 0.6, "continue": 0.8}
ASSIGN_VALUE = 0.75
WALRUS_VALUE = 0.6
LINE_BREAK = re.compile(r"\\n|\n")
GUTTER = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+\t")
CODE_PUNCT = re.compile(r"[{};()=\[\]]")
# A simple left-hand side, optionally after a declaration keyword.
ASSIGN_LHS = re.compile(r"^\s*((const|let|var|val|final|static|int)\s+)?[A-Za-z_][\w.\[\]]*\s*$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    line = "" if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1]
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = tok.strip()
    before = GUTTER.sub("", LINE_BREAK.split(line)[-1])
    value = 0.0
    if word in KEYWORD and (before.strip() == "" or CODE_PUNCT.search(before)):
        value = KEYWORD[word]
    elif word == "=" and ASSIGN_LHS.match(before):
        value = ASSIGN_VALUE
    elif word == ":=":
        value = WALRUS_VALUE
    return (doc, (line + tok)[-400:]), value

        'sommes êtes était étaient étais fut furent sera seront serait '

    ),

        'peut peuvent peux puis pouv pourra pourrait sav save sais sait '
        'dev doi doit doivent vo voi vois voit voy fais fait font fer '
        'fera dit dis prend rend comprend entend attend met sort part '

    ),

ENDINGS = {
 'imperfect':'ait aient ais iez',
 'past':'it ut ît',
 'future':'ra ront rais rait era eront tra',
 'plural':'ent ient nt ont ons ions ez',
 'participle':'ant',

ENDING_OF = {w:g for g,ws in ENDINGS.items() for w in ws.split()}
# (baseline, French context, recent subject, apostrophe)

    'avoir_ont': (0.0, 3.0, 0.7, 0.0),
    'avoir_other': (0.0, 1.2, 1.2, 0.1),
    'etre_est': (0.0, 1.3, 2.0, 0.6),
    'etre_suis': (1.5, 1.0, 2.1, 0.0),
    'etre_sont': (1.1, 0.6, 0.7, 0.0),
    'etre_other': (0.0, 1.2, 1.1, 0.3),
    'finite_verbs': (0.0, 1.7, 1.7, 0.0),
    'adverb_y': (0.0, 1.1, 2.5, 2.2),
    'negation_n': (0.0, 0.9, 1.5, -0.1),
    'clitics': (0.0, 0.4, 0.7, 0.0),
    'imperfect': (0.0, 1.2, 1.4, 0.0),
    'past': (0.0, 1.7, 1.6, 0.0),
    'future': (0.0, 2.1, 0.7, 0.0),
    'plural': (0.0, 0.9, 0.4, 0.0),
    'participle': (0.0, 0.2, 0.0, 0.0),
    'future_ai': (0.0, 1.9, 0.9, 0.0),
    'verb_a': (0.0, 0.9, 0.4, 0.0),
    'present_is': (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.0),
    'present_stems': (0.0, 1.7, 0.5, 0.0),
}

def category(token):
    w = token.strip().lower().strip("'’")
    boundary = token.startswith((' ',"'",'’'))
    if boundary:
        return GROUP_OF.get(w)
    return ENDING_OF.get(w)

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        language, subject, previous, older = 0.0, 0.0, '', ''

    subject = max(subject*.65, new_subject)
    return (doc, language, subject, word, previous), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1358 -- a French "verb right after its subject" detector.

It fires on the conjugated verb (or auxiliary) that follows a subject in French text,
strongest on the 3rd-person forms of avoir / être in "il y a", "n'a", "il est", "qui a",
"elle est", and on the "y" of "il y". Silent in English and code.

How it decides, per token (only the prefix is read):
  1. "French context": at least 3 common French function words in the 8 tokens before.
  2. "subject": the previous token is a subject pronoun (il, elle, qui, on, ils, je, nous, ...).
  3. Cells, first match wins (values are the mean activation of each cell on training text):
     - "y" after a subject pronoun ("il y")                      -> 8.5
     - "a"/"est"/... after "y" that follows a subject ("il y a") -> 7.0
     - elided "'a", "'est", "'y" after n / ne ("n'a")             -> 5.7
     - finite avoir/être/aller/pouvoir/faire form after a subject -> 3.2
     - finite form in French context, any previous token           -> 1.8
     - any token after a subject in French context                 -> 1.0
     - everything else                                             -> 0.0

Main point: the component marks the verb slot of a French clause, with the 3sg
avoir/être forms carrying the largest values. It does not capture verb identity beyond
that list, nor the small negative values on word fragments in other text.
"""

READS = ()

SUBJECTS = {" il", " Il", "il", "Il", "'il", "’il", " elle", " Elle", " qui", " On", "On", " ce",
            " ils", " je", " Je", " nous", " vous", " Nous", " Vous", " elles", " tu", " Tu"}
FR_WORDS = {"le", "la", "les", "de", "des", "du", "et", "que", "qui", "il", "elle", "ils", "elles",
            "on", "ne", "pas", "un", "une", "est", "sont", "au", "aux", "en", "dans", "pour", "sur",
            "ce", "cette", "ces", "nous", "vous", "je", "tu", "se", "sa", "son", "ses", "leur",
            "mais", "ou", "avec", "par", "plus", "à", "était", "qu", "n", "d", "l", "c", "y", "ont",
            "fait", "peut"}
Y = {" y", "'y", "’y"}
FINITE = {" a", "'a", "’a", " est", "'est", "’est", " ont", " sont", " avait", " était", " sera",
          " peut", " fait", " va", " fut", " avons", " avez", " avaient", " étaient", " seront",
          " peuvent", " font", " doit", " doivent", " vont"}
ELIDED = {"'a", "’a", "'est", "’est", "'ai", "’ai", "'y", "’y", "'était"}
NEG = {" n", " ne", "n", "ne"}


def is_french(tokens):
    """At least 3 French function words among the given tokens."""
    count = sum(t.strip().lower().replace("’", "'") in FR_WORDS for t in tokens)
    return count >= 3


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings
    cur = s[-1]
    prev = s[-2] if len(s) > 1 else ""
    prev2 = s[-3] if len(s) > 2 else ""
    subj = prev in SUBJECTS
    if cur in Y and subj:
        return None, 8.5
    if cur in FINITE and prev in Y and prev2 in SUBJECTS:
        return None, 7.0
    if cur in ELIDED and prev in NEG:
        return None, 5.7
    if cur in FINITE and subj:
        return None, 3.2

    return None, 0.0

What it responds to, in plain terms: a few programming keywords, and the `.com` of a GitHub
address, each where code puts it.

- `new` that opens an object creation: right after `=`, `throw`, `return` or `(`
  (`Scanner s = new Scanner(...)`, `throw new Error(...)`): about 1.0. After an indent or a
  comma it is weaker (about 0.2). The word after prose ("a new", "the new") does nothing.
- `.com` right after `github` (`https://github.com/...`, Go imports `github.com/...`): about 1.6.
- `return` as a statement, at the start of a line or after `{`, `}`, `)`, `;`: about 0.5.
  The word in prose ("will return") does nothing.
- `import` after a `;` (a statement boundary, as in Java, JS or Go): about 0.5; otherwise 0.1.
- Small effects: `=` and the common function words (the, of, and, a, to, in, is, ...) are
  slightly negative. The first token of a document (the first token after `<|endoftext|>`,
  or a capitalised one) is negative, about -0.17.

Everything else predicts 0. The program reads only the current token, the one before it, and
whether a new document has just started: the context resets there, as the model's attention does.
"""

READS = ()

NEW_AFTER = ("=", "throw", "return", "(")
WEAK_NEW_AFTER = ("", "\n", ",", "\t")
STATEMENT_BEFORE_RETURN = ("", "{", "}", ")", ";", "]")
FUNCTION_WORDS = ("the", "of", "and", "a", "to", "in", "is", "with", "as", "it", "or", "an", "by")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        # first token of a document has no context: only its own identity matters
        if prefix.position > 0 and prefix.token_strings[-2] == "<|endoftext|>":
            return carry, -0.17
        return carry, -0.1 if cur[:1].isupper() else 0.0
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if cur in ("new", "(new", "=new", "\tnew", ".New"):
        if prev in NEW_AFTER:
            return carry, 1.0

            return carry, 0.2
        return carry, 0.0
    if cur == ".com" and prev.endswith("github"):
        return carry, 1.6
    if cur == "return" and prev in STATEMENT_BEFORE_RETURN:
        return carry, 0.5
    if cur == "import":
        return carry, 0.5 if prev == ";" else 0.1
    if cur == "=":
        return carry, -0.05
    if cur in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return carry, -0.01
    return carry, 0.0

What it does, in plain terms:
  1. Document starts. The first token of a document has no earlier context, so the

    current = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()

"""Negative activation inside formal proof text (Isabelle / Lean / formal maths).

What it does. The component writes a negative amount into the residual stream
when the text is a formal proof or a formal statement. It is near zero in
ordinary prose and code. Inside formal text it goes negative, and the more
formal words there are nearby, the more negative it gets.

For each token it counts the formal words among the last WINDOW tokens of the
same document (the token itself included). Formal words are proof-script words
("by", "simp", "have", "apply", "rw", "intro", "exact", "tactic", "goal", "case",
...), proof marks ("✝", "⊢", "›"), Isabelle escapes ("\\<...>") and formal-maths
words ("Type", "Prop", "Set", "Nat", "ℕ", "ℝ", "∀", "∃", "∈", "inst...").
If the count is above THRESHOLD and the token is formal notation (a colon,
bracket, "=", "<", ">", "→", or a formal word), the prediction is
SCALE * (count - THRESHOLD). Otherwise it is 0. Plain English words inside a
proof stay near zero.

Why. In proof scripts the activation is often -2 to -10 and grows with how
dense the formal text is around it. A count of formal words over a window is
the simplest readable proxy for "how deep in formal text are we".
"""

from collections import deque

READS = ()
WINDOW = 120
THRESHOLD = 3
SCALE = -0.24

FORMAL_WORDS = {
    "by", "have", "simp", "auto", "apply", "rw", "intro", "exact", "tactic", "goal",
    "goals", "case", "theorem", "lemma", "moreover", "ultimately", "fastforce", "blast",
    "unfolding", "thesis", "OF", "add", "using", "show", "sorry", "qed", "obtain",
    "✝", "⊢", "›", "‹", "Type", "Prop", "Set", "Nat", "ℕ", "ℝ", "∀", "∃", "∈",
}
NOTATION = {":", "::", ":=", "(", "[", '"', "=", "<", ">", "→", "⊆"}


def is_formal_word(word):
    return word in FORMAL_WORDS or word.startswith(("inst", "\\<", ">\\<"))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    if carry is None or len(docs) < 2 or docs[-2] != docs[-1]:
        recent = deque(maxlen=WINDOW)  # a new document starts: forget the old one
    else:
        recent = carry
    recent.append(is_formal_word(word))
    count = sum(recent)
    if count <= THRESHOLD or not (word in NOTATION or is_formal_word(word)):
        return recent, 0.0
    return recent, SCALE * (count - THRESHOLD)

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Mostly silent. It fires on about 0.03% of positions, and its typical value is
    near zero, so the program predicts only its two main, reproducible tendencies:
  1. The first token of each document (the token right after <|endoftext|>, or the
     first token of a row) tends to be negative, about -0.16. At a document start the
     model has no earlier context, so the value depends mostly on that token.
  2. Non-Latin "syllable" characters (Hangul, Thai, kana) get a small positive value,
     +0.03, and a replacement character (U+FFFD, a byte fragment that does not decode
     alone) gets +0.04 when it sits among other replacement characters in the last
     8 tokens of the same document, and +0.003 otherwise. These are the
     mis-decoded or mixed-script stretches where the component is most often active.
Everything else is 0. The rare large spikes (up to about +9, on Korean, Thai and
kana syllables inside garbled text) are not predicted, so the variance explained is
close to zero. Its job in the model is small: switching it off changes the next-token
distribution by about 1e-5 nats per position.

REPLACEMENT = "�"
SYLLABLE_SCRIPTS = ("HANGUL", "THAI", "HIRAGANA", "KATAKANA")
DOC_START = -0.16
SYLLABLE = 0.03
GARBLED = 0.04
GARBLED_WINDOW = 8


def _script(token: str) -> str:
    """Unicode script of a token's first character, e.g. 'HANGUL' ('' if none)."""
    if not token:
        return ""
    return unicodedata.name(token[0], "").split(" ")[0]

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_ids) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != doc:
        return carry, DOC_START
    lo = max(0, len(prefix.token_ids) - GARBLED_WINDOW - 1)
    recent = [
        s

        if d == doc

        garbled = any(REPLACEMENT in s for s in recent)
        return carry, GARBLED if garbled else 0.003
    if _script(token) in SYLLABLE_SCRIPTS:

    return carry, 0.0

  the `<` bound, `range(`, `len(` and `of` in the same header, and the `:` of a Java
  `for (T x : xs)` header.

- Text that was mis-decoded from UTF-8 (Latin-1 letters `Ã`, `ã`, and the broken-byte

training text, not fitted per token.

    " await": 1.2, " async": 0.4, " typeof": 2.3, "typeof": 2.5, " isinstance": 1.3,
    " hasattr": 1.2, " len": 0.8, "(len": 1.1, " range": 0.5, " enumerate": 1.0,
    " mut": 0.7, "mut": 1.0, " ∈": 0.8, "∈": 0.7, " foreach": 0.4,

MOJIBAKE_MARKS = ("Ã", "Â", "ã")

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    first = len(prefix) == 1 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]

    else:
        line, recent = carry
    line = "" if "\n" in tok else line + tok
    head = line.lstrip(" \t")
    in_for = head.startswith("for ") and ":" not in head
    in_java_for = head.startswith("for (") and ")" not in head

    value = 0.0

"""Approximate this component with S-initial spelling and local alliteration.

Transliterate spelling, recognize new S-words and pieces of an unfinished
S-word, and keep fading counts of recent S spellings. Capital S and S alone
are stronger; common grammatical S-words are weaker. Initial letter pairs
provide small spelling adjustments. There is a small response just after an
S-token, larger before 'of', and a negative document-start offset. All state
resets at document boundaries. This deliberately omits the component's token-specific irregularities.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii

GRAMMAR_WORDS = frozenset('''she should shall so some such same since still
several somebody someone something somehow somewhere sometimes'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def spelling(token):
    text = anyascii(token).lower()
    words = re.findall('[a-z]+', text)
    return text, words[0] if words else '', words


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    fresh = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    if fresh:
        carry = (doc, None, 0., 0., 0., 0.)
    _, word_s, previous_s, previous_start, recent_s, recent_start = carry
    text, word, words = spelling(token)
    starts_s = word.startswith('s')
    continuing = bool(text and text[0].isalpha() and word_s is not None)
    continues_s = continuing and word_s
    new_s = starts_s and not continuing
    recent_s = min(recent_s, 4.)
    recent_start = min(recent_start, 4.)
    initial = text.lstrip()

    value = -0.006 - 0.169 * fresh
    value += 0.109 * new_s
    value += 0.183 * (new_s and text.strip() == 's')
    value += 0.094 * token.lstrip().startswith('S')
    value += 0.029 * initial.startswith('st')
    value += 0.066 * initial.startswith('sp')
    value += 0.067 * initial.startswith('sa')

    value -= 0.050 * bool(starts_s and text and
                         not text[0].isalnum() and not text[0].isspace())
    value += starts_s * (0.044 * previous_s + 0.119 * recent_start)
    if continues_s:
        value += 0.063 + 0.083 * recent_s + 0.067 * previous_start
    value += 0.027 * previous_start
    value += 0.145 * (previous_start and word == 'of')

            word_s = words[-1].startswith('s')
    else:

    carry = (doc, word_s, count, float(starts_s),

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:1367 -- an "s-sound word" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: this component switches on for words that begin with
the letter S (or another s-sound letter: Cyrillic с, Greek sigma, Arabic sin/shin).
Its strongest response is on the first piece of such a word, a bit stronger when the
word is capitalised ("System", "State", "San", "Saint", " S"). It also fires on the
later pieces of such a word when the word is split into several tokens ("Stas|ys",
"s|ash", "Sch|olar"), and on " of" right after an s-word ("state of", "system of").
Words that start with other letters, and s-letters in the middle of a word, stay near
zero. The first token of a document (right after <|endoftext|>, or the first token of
a row) is pushed slightly negative unless it is an s-word.

The program keeps no state: at each position it looks back over the current document
only to find the start of the word the token belongs to.
"""

READS = ()

S_SOUND = set("sSсСσςسش")


def _lead(token):
    """The first letter of a token, after any leading spaces or punctuation."""
    return token.lstrip(" \t\n\"(_-./[{")[:1]


def _s_word(strs, t, start):
    """Whether the word token t belongs to starts with an s-sound, and where that word starts.

    The word is the run of letter-tokens ending at t: each piece after the first has no
    leading space and follows a piece that ends in a letter. `start` is the document's first token."""
    k = t
    while k > start and strs[k][:1].isalpha() and not strs[k][:1].isspace() and strs[k - 1][-1:].isalpha():
        k -= 1
    return _lead(strs[k]) in S_SOUND, k


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    strs = prefix.token_strings
    start = t
    while start > 0 and docs[start - 1] == docs[t]:
        start -= 1  # first token of this token's document
    if t == start:
        return carry, (0.28 if _lead(strs[t]) in S_SOUND else -0.18)
    if not _lead(strs[t]).isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0  # digits, punctuation, spaces: no response
    is_s, k = _s_word(strs, t, start)
    if is_s:
        value = (0.13, 0.28, 0.19)[min(t - k, 2)]  # first piece, second piece, later pieces
        if _lead(strs[k]).isupper():
            value += 0.1  # capitalised word
        return carry, value
    if strs[t] == " of" and t > start and _s_word(strs, t - 1, start)[0]:
        return carry, 0.25  # "of" right after an s-word, as in "state of"
    return carry, 0.0

"""Approximate a response to capital-letter fragments in symbolic text.

Single capitals get stronger predictions in passages with many capital
letters or operators/brackets. Pronoun I and continued acronym letters
get less; bracket-attached and mathematical styled capitals get more.
Underscore and hyphen prefixes weaken the response. Multi-letter capitals
have a weaker version of the context response. A small length-dependent
adjustment applies at document starts. All context resets at documents.

SYMBOLS = frozenset('$=+*/<>({[')

    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    previous, recent = ('', []) if start else carry[1:]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = token.strip()
    letters = ''.join(c for c in s if c.isalpha())
    first = next((i for i, c in enumerate(s) if c.isalpha()), len(s))
    before = s[:first]
    space = token[:1].isspace()
    joined = not (space or before) and previous[-1:].isupper()
    symbolic = min(sum(item[1] for item in recent), 5) / 5
    capitals = min(sum(item[0] for item in recent), 8) / 8
    single = len(letters) == 1 and letters.isupper()
    caps = len(letters) > 1 and letters.isupper()

    value = -0.002
    if single:
        value += 0.23 + 0.39 * symbolic + 0.29 * capitals
        if joined:
            value -= 0.24
        if s == 'I':
            value -= 0.21
        if letters in ('X', 'Y', 'Z'):  # coordinate-letter convention
            value += 0.08
        if before[-1:] in ('(', '[', '{', '<'):
            value += 0.36
        if before.startswith('_'):
            value -= 0.26
        if before.startswith('-'):
            value -= 0.07
        styled = any('MATHEMATICAL' in unicodedata.name(c, '') for c in s)
        if styled:
            value += 1.27
        elif not s.isascii():
            value -= 0.23
    elif caps:
        value += 0.06 + 0.07 * symbolic + 0.27 * capitals
        if joined:
            value -= 0.12
    elif len(letters) == 1 and letters.islower():
        value -= 0.01

    if (not space and previous[-1:].isupper() and letters
            and not single and not caps):
        value -= 0.035
    if start:
        value += 0.033 * min(len(letters), 12)

                        any(c in SYMBOLS for c in s))])[-32:]

"""Recognize n/н joining a consonant cluster in a word fragment.

The response depends on the preceding consonant's class and is stronger for
Cyrillic fragments. A short vowel fragment immediately after such a cluster
can retain the response. Repeated middle dots give a positive response.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()
VOWELS = set('aeiouyаеёиоуыэюяіїє')
NASALS = set('mnмн')
LIQUIDS = set('lrлрьъwjй')
STOPS = set('bpdktgбпдктг')
N = set('nн')
# Fitted amplitudes for these spelling classes, not for particular tokens.
VALUES = {
    'latin_stop': -1.965,
    'latin_other': -1.121,
    'latin_digraph': -2.898,
    'latin_nasal': -0.73,
    'latin_liquid': -0.465,
    'cyrillic_stop': -3.172,
    'cyrillic_other': -2.414,
    'cyrillic_nasal': -1.478,
    'cyrillic_liquid': -1.327,
    'cyrillic_double_n': -0.464,
    'inside_cluster': -0.4,
    'after_cluster': -0.981,
    'dots': 3.165,
}



def plain(text):
    return ''.join(c for c in unicodedata.normalize('NFD', text.lower())
                   if not unicodedata.combining(c))


def spelling_class(s, prev, tail):
    if s == '··' and prev == s:
        return 'dots', 1.0
    if not s.isalpha():
        return None, 0.0
    last = tail[-1:]
    if s.startswith(('n', 'н')) and last:
        cyr = s.startswith('н')
        script = 'cyrillic_' if cyr else 'latin_'
        scale = 1.0
        if len(s) >= (5 if cyr else 4):
            scale *= 0.6 if cyr else 0.25
        if last in N:
            return ('cyrillic_double_n', scale) if cyr and len(s) > 2 else (None, 0.0)
        if last in VOWELS:
            return None, 0.0
        if last in NASALS:
            return script + 'nasal', scale
        if last in LIQUIDS:
            return script + 'liquid', scale
        if not cyr and prev.endswith(('ch', 'sh')):
            return 'latin_digraph', scale
        if len(prev) < 2 or not prev[-2].isalpha():
            scale *= 0.5
        return script + ('stop' if last in STOPS else 'other'), scale
    if (2 <= len(s) <= 3 and s[-1] in N
            and all(c not in VOWELS for c in s)
            and s[-2] not in NASALS | LIQUIDS):
        return 'inside_cluster', 1.0
    if (len(s) <= 3 and s[0] in VOWELS and last in N
            and len(tail) > 1 and tail[-2] not in VOWELS | NASALS | LIQUIDS):
        return 'after_cluster', 1.0
    return None, 0.0


def update_tail(s, tail):
    if s.isalpha():
        return (tail + s)[-3:]
    i = len(s)
    while i and s[i - 1].isalpha():
        i -= 1
    return s[i:][-3:]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev, tail = carry[1:] if carry and carry[0] == doc else ('', '')
    s = plain(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    kind, scale = spelling_class(s, prev, tail)
    value = scale * VALUES.get(kind, 0.0)
    return (doc, s, update_tail(s, tail)), value

The component goes negative on a word-final suffix piece that the tokenizer split off
from its stem, when the piece is an n-initial inflectional ending:

* Russian adjective endings -ный, -ной, -ного, -ные, -ным, -ных, -ная, -ное ... fire

  participle such as созданного) stays near zero.
* Polish/Czech/German n-endings (-ner, -ní, -né, -ny, -nych ... after a stem of three
  or more letters) fire about -2; -na, -ne, -no about -0.8. Uppercase and short
  stems do not fire.
* A bare n inside a non-English word with diacritics (Leś|n|iki, Kort|n|ema) fires
  weakly.

It is zero everywhere else: in particular when the ending is part of a larger token
(выпускной as one token), at word starts, and for most English or code text. Some
English-like fragments (-ne, -na after a stem) still get the weak Latin value.

The program predicts those values from the current token and the word before it,
using only the prefix. It carries no state.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

# Russian adjective endings that begin with н, and nominal/adverbial н-endings.
ADJ_ENDINGS = ("ными", "ного", "ному", "ным", "ные", "ный", "ной", "ную", "ное",
               "ная", "ном", "ных", "ней", "них", "ний", "ним")
NOUN_ENDINGS = ("ность", "ности", "ностью", "ник", "ня", "но", "ни", "ну", "н")

# Polish / Czech / German n-endings written in Latin letters.
LATIN_STRONG = ("ner", "nej", "né", "ní", "ni", "ny", "nych", "nam", "nie")
LATIN_WEAK = ("na", "ne", "no", "nes", "net", "nu")

    text = prefix.text_prefixes[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    if not token or token[0].isspace():
        return carry, 0.0

    if re.fullmatch(r"[а-яё]+", token):

        word = re.search(r"[а-яё]*$", text.lower()).group(0)
        is_ending = token in ADJ_ENDINGS or token in NOUN_ENDINGS

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]

    doc_start = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if raw == DOT_RUN:

"""Large positive responses to document-opening source code and headings.

Recognize file declarations, imports, comment/docstring delimiters, Markdown
headings and markup starts. Exact delimiter spelling matters: a newline joined
to // is not itself the strong signal, but a following // is. An uninterrupted
run of the same opening token keeps its opening value. Predict zero elsewhere,
omitting the component's much smaller, varied lexical responses.
"""
READS = ()

# Familiar source-file and document-opening syntax, with calibrated amplitudes.
OPENERS = {
    'package': 2.98,
    'from': 2.74,
    'import': 1.75,
    'use': 1.56,
    'using': 1.10,
    'def': 1.18,
    'const': 1.06,
    '//': 2.76,
    '/*': 2.13,
    '/*\n': 2.60,
    '/*\r\n': 2.57,
    '#': 2.44,
    '##': 1.96,
    '###': 0.59,
    '#!/': 1.44,
    '#pragma': 0.85,
    '#ifndef': 0.85,
    '#include': 0.32,
    '<': 1.13,
    '<?': 0.70,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        opening = token
    else:
        opening = carry[1]
        if opening == '//\n' and token == '//':

usually inside a Greek word that is spelled out in fragments. Replacement-character
fragments (U+FFFD) sometimes give positive spikes, but on average they give nothing a
simple rule can use.

What this program does: it predicts a fixed negative value on those Greek letters and 0
on every other token. The token's own identity is the only input. The context that decides
when a spike happens is not captured, so this program explains only a small part of the
variance.

"""A local conversational/direct-speech signal.

questions, contractions and response words gain strength near the beginning of
quoted speech, speaker labels, greetings and vocative commas. State consists of
textual speech cues, resets at document boundaries, and never reads future text.
For example, "Wait, maybe" and "Hello! I" build a short speech cue;
ordinary content words receive only a tiny share of it.
"""
import math
READS = ()
# role: (words, ordinary baseline, sensitivity to conversational cues)
GROUPS = {
    'other': ('', -0.0035, 0.0568),
    'speaker': ('I', -0.0076, 1.9686),
    'addressee': ('you', -0.0383, 2.3394),
    'speaker_object': ('me', 0.1098, 1.4607),
    'possessive_address': ('my your', -0.0277, 1.0258),
    'inclusive': ('we us our', 0.0002, 0.7243),
    'demonstrative': ('that this', -0.0053, 0.8962),
    'deictic': ('it there here', -0.0153, 0.4847),
    'question': ('what why how who where when', 0.0191, 1.0452),
    'uncertainty': ('maybe perhaps', 0.9981, 1.4204),
    'reflection': ('hmm hm', 1.1619, 0.8593),
    'interjection': ('ah oh uh um huh eh wait', 0.0627, 1.1219),
    'greeting': ('hello hi hey goodbye', -0.0327, 1.3627),
    'agreement': ('yes yeah yep okay ok indeed fine', -0.0737, 1.3201),
    'response': ('well no nope sure right', -0.0571, 1.1567),
    'social': ("thanks thank please sorry sir madam ma'am excuse", 0.2584, 1.3737),
    'auxiliary': (
        'do does did are is am can could would will shall should have has may',
        -0.0172, 0.4112),
    'contrast': ('but', -0.0241, 1.1172),
    'transition': ('and so now then not', -0.0126, 0.4445),
    'conversation_frame': (
        'think see know mean want going really actually',
        -0.0020, 1.2117),
    'contraction': ("'s", 0.0073, 1.0783),
    'han_address': ('我 你 您 你们 你們 我们 我們', 0.2870, 2.2069),
    'han_particle': ('啊 呀 哦 喂 呃 嗯 吧 吗 嗎 呢', 0.8692, 2.4335),
    'han_discourse_word': ('这 這 那 怎么 怎麼 什么 什麼 好', 0.2898, 1.7806),
    'comma': ('', -0.0025, 0.7025),
    'colon': ('', -0.0203, 0.2540),
    'exclamation': ('', 0.1114, 0.8486),
    'question_mark': ('', -0.0465, 1.1033),
    'ellipsis': ('', 0.3074, 1.4004),
    'period': ('', 0.0016, 0.2183),
    'quote': ('', -0.0606, 0.0956),
    'common_ground': ('', 0.7696, 1.2696),
    'suggestion': ('', 0.6505, 0.4269),
    'encouragement': ('', 1.9147, 1.0690),
    'courtesy': ('', 0.8128, 2.2720),
    'personal_contraction': ('', -0.0573, 1.1315),
    'negative_contraction': ('', -0.0662, 0.8721),
}
CLASSES = {w: name for name, (words, _, _) in GROUPS.items()
           for w in words.split()}
ENGLISH_ROLES = {name for name, (words, _, _) in GROUPS.items()
                 if words and not name.startswith('han_')
                 and name != 'contraction'}

def observe(carry, s, doc):
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, '', '', 1000, 0, '', 0., 1000, 0., False, False, 0.)
    (_, prev, tail, age, line_n, line, opener,
     speaker_age, greeting, line_quote, dialogue, hesitation) = carry
    w = s.strip().lower().replace('’', "'")
    boundary = s[:1].isspace() or not tail[-1:].isalnum()
    key = 'I' if s.strip() == 'I' else w
    cls = CLASSES.get(key, 'other')
    if key == 'i': cls = 'other'  # lowercase i is commonly a variable, not English I.
    if not boundary and cls in ENGLISH_ROLES: cls = 'other'
    if w in (',', '，'): cls = 'comma'
    elif w in (':', '：'): cls = 'colon'
    elif w and all(c in '!！' for c in w): cls = 'exclamation'
    elif w and all(c in '?？' for c in w): cls = 'question_mark'
    elif w in ('…', '……', '...', '··'): cls = 'ellipsis'
    elif w == '.': cls = 'period'
    elif w in ('"', '“', '”', '「', '」', '『', '』'): cls = 'quote'
    # Familiar conversational constructions, including split words.
    before = tail.lower().rstrip()
    if w == 'course' and before.endswith('of'): cls = 'common_ground'
    if (w == 'about' and before.endswith('how') or
            w == 'see' and before.endswith("let's")): cls = 'suggestion'
    if w == 'on' and before.endswith('come'): cls = 'encouragement'
    if (w == 'me' and before.endswith(('excuse','allow')) or
            w == 'you' and before.endswith('thank')): cls = 'courtesy'
    if w in ("'m", "'re", "'ll", "'d", "'ve"): cls = 'personal_contraction'
    if w == "'t": cls = 'negative_contraction'
    # Opening ASCII quotes are inferred from the preceding character, not parity:
    # a row can begin midway through a quotation.
    closed = False
    opening = any(c in s for c in '“「『')
    for j,ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch == '"' or (ch == "'" and w == "'"):
            before = (tail+s[:j])[-1:]
            if not before or before.isspace() or before in '([{:=':
                opening = True
            else:
                closed = True
    if opening:
        age = 0
        line_quote = (line_n == 0 or not line.strip())
    label = (w in (':', '：') and 0 < line_n <= 5
             and line.strip()[:1].isupper() and not any(c.isdigit() for c in line))
    if label:
        speaker_age = 0
        if line.strip().lower() in ('user','assistant','human','bot','narrator'):
            dialogue = True
    if speaker_age <= 3 and cls in (
            'speaker', 'addressee', 'speaker_object', 'question',
            'interjection', 'greeting', 'agreement', 'response', 'social'):
        dialogue = True
    quote_recency = math.exp(-age / 12)
    speaker_recency = math.exp(-speaker_age / 10)
    speech = max(quote_recency, speaker_recency)
    pclass = CLASSES.get(prev, 'other')
    comma = prev in (',', '，')
    auxiliary = pclass == 'auxiliary'
    pronoun = pclass in ('speaker', 'addressee', 'speaker_object',
                         'possessive_address', 'inclusive')
    address_question = (
        cls == 'addressee' and prev in ('do','did','are','were','have') or
        w in ('do','did','are','were','have') and
        prev in ('what','how','why','where'))
    first_person_inversion = (
        cls == 'speaker' and prev in ('may','can','could','shall','should'))
    # Speech openings, punctuation, discourse markers, and question forms.
    strength = (
        .8802*quote_recency + .7583*speaker_recency
        + .3470*line_quote*quote_recency + 1.0770*(label and dialogue)
        + .0479*comma + .2029*(prev in (':','：'))
        + .2080*('!' in prev or '！' in prev)
        + .6007*(pclass in ('reflection','interjection'))
        + .1076*pronoun + .0014*auxiliary
        + .2426*opener + .6654*greeting + .9256*hesitation
        + speech*(.8331*comma + .3797*auxiliary + .5818*pronoun)
        + .3399*address_question + .3172*first_person_inversion
    )
    if closed or any(c in s for c in '”」』'):
        age = 1000
    opener = max(opener * .75, float(cls in (
        'uncertainty','reflection','interjection','greeting','agreement','response')))
    hesitation = max(hesitation * .75, float(cls in ('reflection', 'interjection')))
    greeting = max(greeting * .8, float(cls == 'greeting'))
    if '\n' in s:
        line_n, line = 0, s.rsplit('\n',1)[-1].strip()
    else:
        line_n += 1
        line = (line + s)[:120]
    state = (doc, 'I' if key=='I' else w, (tail+s)[-48:], age+1,
             line_n, line, opener, speaker_age+1, greeting, line_quote,
             dialogue, hesitation)
    return state, cls, strength


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    carry, role, strength = observe(
        carry, prefix.token_strings[-1], prefix.document_ids[-1])
    _, baseline, sensitivity = GROUPS[role]
    return carry, float(baseline + sensitivity * strength)

"""Word-fragment detector for the spelling "h-a-l" / "h-a-b" (and friends).

A layer-1 MLP unit that reads the letters of the current word so far. It is
positive on pieces of words that spell "hal-" or "hab-" (hal, halt, halten, thal,
hab, Hall, Mahal), more so when the piece is a continuation of a word rather than
a whole common word, and strongly negative on frequency and chemistry
abbreviations ending in h-z, h-g or -ertz (Hz, GHz, MHz, Hertz, mmHg). Everything
else is ~0.
"""
import re

from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()

NEG_UNITS = re.compile(r"(hz|hg|ertz|herz)$")
POS_HAL = re.compile(r"h(al|ab|äl)")
MILD_NEG = re.compile(r"h(op|oc|of|og)")
MILD_POS = re.compile(r"h(au|th|ol|old|äl)")


def word_so_far(prefix):
    """Lower-cased letters of the current word, from its first piece to this token."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    pieces = []
    i = len(prefix.token_ids) - 1
    while i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == doc:
        text = prefix.token_strings[i]
        core = text.lstrip(" ")
        if not core.isalpha():
            break
        pieces.append(core.lower())
        if core != text:  # a leading space: this piece starts the word
            break
        i -= 1
    return "".join(reversed(pieces))


def is_common_word(text):
    return max(zipf_frequency(text, "en"), zipf_frequency(text, "de")) >= 4.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = word_so_far(prefix)
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if NEG_UNITS.search(word):
        return carry, -4.0
    if POS_HAL.search(word):
        # A whole common word that starts here (" half", " habit") stays quiet.
        if token.startswith(" ") and is_common_word(token.strip().lower()):
            return carry, 0.3
        return carry, 1.2
    if MILD_NEG.search(word):
        return carry, -0.5
    if MILD_POS.search(word):
        return carry, 0.2
    return carry, 0.0

A negative detector for the word "size" in any form. It goes strongly negative on the
newest token when that token is part of "size": " size", " sizes", "Size", "sized",
"resize", "_size", ".size", "sizeof", and the capital forms "SIZES", "_SIZE". It also
fires when the word is split across tokens: the text so far, with spaces and underscores
removed and lowercased, has just spelled "size" or "sizes" (e.g. "samples" + "ize" ->
"samplesize", or "FREE_LIST_S" + "IZES"). Plain words are about -3.5, code fragments about
-2.6, capitals and split words about -6, the short form "sz" -1. Everywhere else it is 0.
"""

READS = ()

PLAIN = -3.5     # " size", "size", " sizes", "sized" (a word, in prose or code)
CODE = -2.6      # "_size", ".size", "-size", "Size", "sizeof" (an identifier piece)
CAPS = -6.0      # "SIZES", "_SIZE" (capitals), or "IZES" completing a split word
SPLIT = -6.0     # a split word completed across a token boundary: "samples" + "ize"

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = token.strip(" _.-\t").lower()
    window = "".join(prefix.token_strings[-3:]).replace(" ", "").replace("_", "").lower()
    value = 0.0
    if "size" in core:
        if token.isupper():
            value = CAPS
        elif token[:1] == " " or core in ("size", "sizes", "sized"):
            value = PLAIN
        else:
            value = CODE
    elif core in ("ize", "izes", "e", "es") and (window.endswith("size") or window.endswith("sizes")):

    elif core == "sz":
        value = -1.0
    return carry, float(value)

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]

"""Estimate a mostly negative 'following material begins here' signal.

Colons are strongest at prose-to-list/explanation boundaries, especially
with a line break. Numerical and programming uses are weaker. These are
surface cues with training-fitted strengths, not a syntax parser.
Other tokens get zero, apart from whitespace following a colon.
Context resets between documents.
"""
import re

READS = ()
BE_FORMS = set('is are was were be been'.split())
LINKING_WORDS = set('to with of that like by from into'.split())
TRANSITIONS = set('so thus then therefore hence example'.split())
HEADINGS = set('observation examples example output input note notes warning '
               'error result results code description'.split())
INTRODUCTION = re.compile(
    r'\b(following|follows|include|includes|including|contain|contains|'
    r'namely|below)\b')
CODE_START = re.compile(
    r'^\s*(?:\d+\s+)?(?:def|class|if|elif|for|while|with|except|else|try)\b')


def response(token, before):
    s = token.replace('：', ':')
    if ':' not in s:
        if not s.strip() and before.rstrip().endswith(':'):
            return -.05 - .50 * (s.count('\n') > 1)
        return 0.0
    i = s.rfind(':')
    left, right = s[:i], s[i+1:]
    if '/' in right or '=' in right or (':' in left and '\n' not in right):
        return 0.0
    if right.strip() not in ('', '\\', '-', '"', "'", '”', '“', '</'):
        return 0.0
    text = before + left
    line = text.split('\n')[-1]
    words = re.findall(r'[^\W\d_]+', line)
    last = words[-1].lower() if words else ''
    n = len(words)
    newlines = right.count('\n')
    newline = newlines > 0 or '\\' in right
    code = bool(CODE_START.search(line))
    symbols = min(sum(line.count(c) for c in '_=;{}'), 3) / 3

    # Prose and line breaks make a stronger opening boundary.
    value = -.11 - .021 * min(n, 12)
    value += .14 * (newlines > 1) - .33 * (newlines > 2)
    if newline:
        value -= .64 + .11 * (n >= 4) + .28 * (last in HEADINGS)
        value += .37 * max(code, symbols)
    # Programming syntax and numeric contexts usually weaken it.
    value += .29 * code + .18 * (':' in line)
    value += .32 * (not text.strip()) - .09 * ('：' in token)
    value += .08 * text.endswith(']') + .10 * text.endswith(' ')
    value += .10 * text.endswith(')') + .08 * ('(' in line)
    value += .12 * (bool(text) and text[-1].isdigit())
    value += .10 * bool(re.search(r'\w_\w*$', text))
    # Words that leave a phrase waiting for its continuation.
    value -= .41 * (last in BE_FORMS) + .35 * (last in LINKING_WORDS)
    value -= .76 * (last == 'as')
    value -= .28 * (last in TRANSITIONS)
    value -= .36 * bool(INTRODUCTION.search(text[-100:].lower()))
    value -= .41 * bool(INTRODUCTION.fullmatch(last))

This component is a negative detector for colons that announce what follows. At a colon
that closes a phrase like "the following:", "including:", "such as:", "as follows:" or
"comprising:", the model expects a list or a block of detail next, and the component goes
strongly negative (about -1.8 for a bare colon, -1.4 for a colon + newline, deepest for
"follows:" or "as follows:" lead-ins). Weaker colons: "of:", "at:", "run:" (about -0.4),
and colons in code (`default:`, `case 6:`, `except ...:`), which are weak or near zero.
Colons after names and citations (`Washington, DC:`, `(Russian:`) are mildly positive
in the data, but the program does not model that and gives them the small default.
Every other token is close to zero, except the first token of a document, which is
slightly positive.

The program reads only the newest token and a short window of the text before it,
and resets that window at each document start.

Predictions, in order:
  * first token of a document: +0.1
  * colon + newline (":\\n", ":\\n\\n", ...): -0.9 in prose, -1.4 after a lead-in phrase
  * bare colon (":", "：", ":\\"): -1.8 after a lead-in phrase, -0.4 after a weak word,
    -0.1 otherwise

  * colon-type predictions are scaled by 0.3 on a code line
  * everything else: 0

    r"(\bfollows?|\bfollowing|\binclud(e|es|ed|ing)|\bsuch as|\bcomprising|\bconsists? of"
    r"|\bas|\bis|\bare|\bwere|\bbelow|\bthese|\bthose|\bas under)\s*$",
    re.I,
)
# lead-in words anywhere in the same sentence, e.g. "the following programs:"
LEAD_SENT = re.compile(r"\b(follow\w*|includ\w*|such as|comprising|comprises|consists? of)\b", re.I)
# prepositions and verbs that often come just before a list-like colon
WEAK_WORD = re.compile(r"\b(of|at|by|on|run|terms|get|got)\s*$", re.I)
# a line of code rather than prose
CODE_LINE = re.compile(
    r"(\b(def|case|default|except|else|elif|if|for|while|return|class|try)\b|[{};=]|<<)"
)

def _activation(recent, tok):
    """`recent`: the text before the current token; `tok`: the current token's text."""
    body = tok.rstrip(" \t\n\\")
    is_colon = body.endswith((":", "："))

        return 0.0

    elif lead:
        value = -1.8
    elif WEAK_WORD.search(before):

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    else:
        recent = carry[0]
    value = _activation(recent, tok)
    if recent == "" and value == 0.0:
        value = 0.1
    return ((recent + tok)[-WINDOW:], doc), float(value)

coarse register heuristic, not an exact account of individual words.

"""
from functools import lru_cache
import re
import regex
import wordnet

READS = ()

NOMINAL = set('tion tions ation ations ion ions ity ities '
              'ization izations'.split())
ADJECTIVE = set('ical ological ative ive ential ary ory ous'.split())
ADVERB = {'ally', 'ically'}
SCIENCE_NOUN_ENDINGS = {'ology', 'ologies', 'ase', 'ases', 'ulus'}
TECHNICAL_PREFIXES = ('bio', 'geo', 'hydro', 'electro', 'thermo',
    'neuro', 'micro', 'nano', 'poly', 'mono', 'anti', 'non', 'trans', 'sub')
FRAGMENTS = NOMINAL | ADJECTIVE | ADVERB | SCIENCE_NOUN_ENDINGS


@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def local_evidence(s):
    w = s.strip()
    low = w.lower()
    word = bool(re.fullmatch('[A-Za-z]+', w))
    frequency = zipf_frequency(low, 'en') if word else 0
    categories = wordnet.categories(low) if word else ()
    scientific_adjective = word and any(
        len(low) > len(end) + 1 and low.endswith(end)
        for end in ('ic', 'ical', 'al'))
    scientific_prefix = word and any(
        len(low) > len(start) + 1 and low.startswith(start)
        for start in TECHNICAL_PREFIXES)

        +0.070 * (word and frequency < 1)
        +0.039 * (word and 1 <= frequency < 4)
        +0.069 * scientific_adjective
        +0.103 * (s in NOMINAL)
        +0.200 * (s in ADJECTIVE)
        +0.330 * (s in ADVERB)
        +0.309 * (s in SCIENCE_NOUN_ENDINGS)
        +0.108 * scientific_prefix
        +0.122 * bool(re.fullmatch('-[a-z]{3,}', w))
        +1.138 * ('[@' in s)
        +0.906 * (w == '-type')
        +0.259 * (low in {'fig', 'figs', 'eq', 'eqs'})
        +1.210 * (low in {'vivo', 'vitro', 'situ', 'silico'})
        +0.084 * (low in {'we', 'our', 'ours', 'us'})
        +0.022 * ('$' in s or '\\' in s)
        +0.019 * bool(regex.search(r'\p{Script=Greek}', w))
        +0.155 * theory
        +0.058 * ('noun.process' in categories)
        +0.031 * ('adj.pert' in categories)

    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    else:
        _, previous, recent, previous_text = carry
    local, word, fragment = local_evidence(s)
    w = s.strip()
    figure_period = s == '.' and previous_text.lower() in {
        'fig', 'figs', 'eq', 'eqs'}
    electron_volt = w == 'V' and previous_text in {
        'e', 'ke', 'Me', 'Ge', 'Te', 'Pe', 'Ee'}

        +0.099 * previous
        -0.051 * recent
        +12.140 * local * recent
        +0.521 * word * recent
        -0.258 * start
        +0.842 * fragment * recent
        +0.175 * figure_period
        +1.399 * electron_volt

    return carry, float(value)
